message.content:
Below is a **complete, ready‑to‑run example** that shows how to launch a Google Cloud Compute Engine instance that has an NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU (if it were available) and runs Ubuntu 20.04 LTS.  
Because Google Cloud does not currently offer the RTX A6000 GPU, the example uses the closest supported GPU type (`nvidia-tesla-a100`) and explains how you would swap it out if the hardware were available.

---

## 1.  Prerequisites

| Item | How to set it up |
|------|------------------|
| **Google Cloud SDK** | `curl https://sdk.cloud.google.com | bash` (or install via your OS package manager) |
| **Authentication** | `gcloud auth login` (or use a service account key) |
| **Project ID** | Replace `<PROJECT_ID>` with your GCP project ID |
| **Zone** | Replace `<ZONE>` with the zone where you want the instance (e.g., `us-central1-a`) |
| **Billing enabled** | Ensure billing is enabled for the project |

---

## 2.  Using the `gcloud` CLI

```bash
# Variables
PROJECT_ID="<PROJECT_ID>"
ZONE="<ZONE>"
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-ubuntu"
MACHINE_TYPE="n1-standard-8"          # 8 vCPU, 30 GB RAM
GPU_TYPE="nvidia-tesla-a100"          # Replace with "nvidia-tesla-a6000" if available
GPU_COUNT=1
IMAGE_FAMILY="ubuntu-2004-lts"
IMAGE_PROJECT="ubuntu-os-cloud"

# Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create $INSTANCE_NAME \
  --project=$PROJECT_ID \
  --zone=$ZONE \
  --machine-type=$MACHINE_TYPE \
  --accelerator=type=$GPU_TYPE,count=$GPU_COUNT \
  --image-family=$IMAGE_FAMILY \
  --image-project=$IMAGE_PROJECT \
  --boot-disk-size=200GB \
  --boot-disk-type=pd-ssd \
  --maintenance-policy=MIGRATE \
  --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform \
  --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh   # optional: custom init script
```

### What each flag does

| Flag | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `--machine-type` | CPU + RAM configuration |
| `--accelerator` | Adds a GPU; replace `nvidia-tesla-a100` with `nvidia-tesla-a6000` if it becomes available |
| `--image-family` & `--image-project` | Pulls the latest Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image |
| `--boot-disk-size` | Size of the boot disk (SSD recommended for GPU workloads) |
| `--scopes` | Grants the instance full Cloud Platform access (needed for GPU drivers) |
| `--metadata-from-file startup-script` | Optional: run a shell script at first boot (e.g., install CUDA, cuDNN, etc.) |

---

## 3.  Using the REST API (JSON)

If you prefer to call the Compute Engine REST API directly (e.g., from a script or a CI/CD pipeline), here’s the exact JSON payload you would POST to:

```http
POST https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/<PROJECT_ID>/zones/<ZONE>/instances
Authorization: Bearer <ACCESS_TOKEN>
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "name": "rtx-a6000-ubuntu",
  "machineType": "zones/<ZONE>/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 200,
        "diskType": "zones/<ZONE>/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "accelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/<PROJECT_ID>/zones/<ZONE>/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a100"
    }
  ],
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"]
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\nsudo apt-get update\nsudo apt-get install -y cuda\n"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

> **Note:**  
> * Replace `<PROJECT_ID>` and `<ZONE>` with your actual values.  
> * Replace `nvidia-tesla-a100` with `nvidia-tesla-a6000` once the GPU becomes available.  
> * The `accessToken` must be obtained via OAuth 2.0 (e.g., `gcloud auth print-access-token`).  

---

## 4.  Post‑Creation Steps

1. **Install GPU Drivers**  
   After the instance boots, SSH into it and run:

   ```bash
   sudo apt-get update
   sudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535   # or the latest driver matching your GPU
   ```

2. **Verify GPU Availability**

   ```bash
   nvidia-smi
   ```

3. **Install CUDA Toolkit & cuDNN**  
   Follow NVIDIA’s official installation guide for Ubuntu 20.04.

4. **Optional: Enable GPU Monitoring**  
   Add the following to your `startup-script` to automatically install `nvidia-docker2` and start a container with GPU support.

---

## 5.  Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Likely Cause | Fix |
|---------|--------------|-----|
| Instance fails to start | GPU type not supported in the selected zone | Check the [GPU availability matrix](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/gpus#availability) and pick a zone that supports the GPU |
| `nvidia-smi` shows no GPUs | Driver not installed or wrong driver version | Reinstall the driver or use the `--metadata-from-file startup-script` to automate it |
| Billing error | Project not linked to a billing account | Link billing via the Cloud Console or `gcloud beta billing projects link` |

---

## 6.  Summary

- **Command‑line**: `gcloud compute instances create ...`  
- **REST API**: POST to `/projects/<PROJECT_ID>/zones/<ZONE>/instances` with JSON body.  
- **GPU**: Use `nvidia-tesla-a100` now; swap to `nvidia-tesla-a6000` when it becomes available.  
- **OS**: Ubuntu 20.04 LTS (image family `ubuntu-2004-lts`).  

Feel free to copy the snippets above into your scripts or CI/CD pipelines. If you hit any snags, let me know!
